close_reason: Applied option (b) per the bead's recommendation: one-line early return on non-object Values before @type dispatch. Now AnniversaryDate::Unknown(json!(scalar | array | null)) round-trips losslessly through serialize→deserialize. Added regression test anniversary_date_unknown_non_object_round_trips with independent oracle (hand-built JSON literals for each non-object shape); verified the test fails without the fix and passes with it. 59 tests pass; pre-commit gate clean. Commit pending.
description: lib.rs:977-997 implements Deserialize for AnniversaryDate by parsing into serde_json::Value first, then dispatching on @type. The Unknown(Value) variant accepts ANY JSON shape — including a scalar like json!("foo") if someone constructs AnniversaryDate::Unknown(...) directly. Serialize at :967-975 forwards verbatim, so back to wire is fine. But on the next deserialize round, the dispatch at :981 does v.get("@type") — which is None for a scalar — and falls through to the PartialDate branch at :990, which fails to parse a scalar as a PartialDate object. Result: a value constructable in Rust cannot survive a serialize→deserialize round trip. This is reachable from Anniversary { date: AnniversaryDate::Unknown(json!("x")), ... }. Suggested rewrite: either (a) restrict the Unknown variant to Value::Object only at construction time (add a from_value constructor that returns Result, make the enum field non-public), or (b) handle non-object values in the deserialize dispatch by routing them to Unknown as well: 'if !v.is_object() { return Ok(AnniversaryDate::Unknown(v)); }' before the @type lookup. Option (b) preserves the round-trip invariant with one line of code.
title: AnniversaryDate::Unknown accepts non-object JSON values it cannot round-trip back
